summary: Robin Coningham works in South Asian archaeology and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin, and held professorships at the University of Bradford (1994–2005) and Durham University (from 2005).
Robin D. S. Yates is a scholar of Sinology and archaeology. He received his PhD from Harvard University around 1980 and held a James McGill Professorship at McGill University beginning around 1993.

Robin Dunbar completed his doctoral studies under John Hurrell Crook after studying at Magdalen College School and Magdalen College. He held an academic post at University College London from around 1987 to 1994.
Roderick Henry Macleod was an Indology scholar who earned an M.A. at the University of Cambridge by 1915 and served there as Lecturer in Indian Law in 1913.

Philosopher Roderick M. Chisholm studied at Brown and Harvard (PhD circa 1942). He taught at the Barnes Foundation (1946) and Brown University (1947–1987), served as president of the Metaphysical Society of America, and edited Philosophy and Phenomenological Research.
Roderick S. Bucknell was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He held a post at the University of Queensland, where he was an Associate Professor around 1999–2000.

Roderick Whitfield works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He held posts at the British Museum (attested 1986), the University of London, and SOAS University of London, where he was Professor Emeritus by 2011.

Roger Billard specialized in Indology, studying at INALCO, the EPHE, and under Louis Renou. He worked in the manuscript department of the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1945–1951) and at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1952–1979).
Roger Bischoff is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teachers Mother Sayamagyi and U Chit Tin, and served as an Assistant Teacher at the International Meditation Centre in 1995.
Roger Brown was a linguist who completed his studies at the University of Michigan between 1945 and 1952. He subsequently served on the faculty at Harvard University from 1962 to 1994.

Roger Goossens was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his PhD at the Université libre de Bruxelles, studying under Émile Boisacq, Paul-Émile Dumont, and Henri Grégoire, and was appointed Professor of Greek there in 1945.

Roger Heim studied at the École Centrale Paris and the Science Faculty of Paris. He served at the Muséum National d'Histoire Naturelle from 1929 to 1970, including as its Director from approximately 1950 to 1965.
Roger Jeffery is an Indology scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Edinburgh in 1985 and served on its faculty from 1972, later becoming Professor Emeritus.

Roger R. Jackson specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He held faculty posts at Fairfield University (1986) and Carleton College (attested 1990–2017).

Sinology and philosophy scholar Roger T. Ames earned his PhD at SOAS under D. C. Lau. He was a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1978–2016) and served as editor of Philosophy East and West.

Rohana Seneviratne studied at the Universities of Peradeniya, Liverpool, and Oxford, where he earned a DPhil in Sanskrit. He held tutoring posts at Liverpool and Oxford, and became Professor of Sanskrit at Peradeniya in 2022.
Rohit Saluja works in the fields of computational studies and Indology, with affiliations at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and BharatGen.

Roland Barthes studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and under Émile Benveniste. He held posts at the CNRS (1953–1959), the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (1962–1976), and the Collège de France (1976–1980).

Roland Ferenczi, an Indology and ancient history scholar, studied at Pécs and Eötvös Loránd University. In 2024, he became an MSCA Postdoctoral Researcher at the University of Hamburg and department head at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences Library.

Roland Grubb Kent studied at Swarthmore and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD 1903). He taught at Pennsylvania (1902–1947), lectured in Sanskrit at Bryn Mawr (1910–1914), and co-founded the Linguistic Society of America in 1924.
